description: Phase 1: Add reply_markup support to send_photo_raw, add send_video_raw, add raw helpers for editing messages (caption, media, reply_markup), add callback query dispatcher to telegram.rs, and add in-memory edit session state to AppState.

steps.task: Add `reply_markup: Option<&str>` parameter to `send_photo_raw` in telegram_notify.rs (line 52). Inside the function body, after building the multipart form, add: `if let Some(markup) = reply_markup { form = form.text("reply_markup", markup.to_owned()); }`. Update both call sites to pass `None`: (1) in `notify_artist_submission` (~line 340) and (2) in `send_show_update_notification` (~line 622).

decisions: Use Option<&str> not serde_json::Value — caller serializes the InlineKeyboardMarkup JSON before passing
reply_markup is passed as a text field in the multipart form, same as caption/parse_mode
learnings: send_photo_raw is at lines 52-100 of telegram_notify.rs (expanded with reply_markup)
Two call sites updated: notify_artist_submission (~L343) and send_show_update_notification (~L625), both pass None
Updated signature: (token, chat_id, photo_bytes, filename, caption, parse_mode, thread_id, reply_markup: Option<&str>) -> Result<i64, String>

steps.task: Add `send_video_raw` function in telegram_notify.rs, modeled after `send_photo_raw`. Signature: `async fn send_video_raw(token: &str, chat_id: i64, video_bytes: Vec<u8>, filename: String, caption: &str, parse_mode: &str, thread_id: Option<i32>, reply_markup: Option<&str>) -> Result<i64, String>`. Uses reqwest::multipart with a `video` part (not `photo`). Calls Telegram `sendVideo` endpoint. Returns message_id from response.

decisions: Same reqwest multipart pattern as send_photo_raw
Part name is 'video' for Telegram sendVideo endpoint
Return message_id for later in-place editing of video messages
learnings: send_audio_raw already exists at lines 99-130+ with similar pattern
TgResponse struct is already defined for parsing Telegram Bot API responses
knowledge.notes: Place after send_photo_raw and before send_audio_raw

steps.task: Add `edit_message_caption_raw` function in telegram_notify.rs. Signature: `pub async fn edit_message_caption_raw(token: &str, chat_id: i64, message_id: i64, caption: &str, parse_mode: &str, reply_markup: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String>`. Uses reqwest JSON POST to Telegram `editMessageCaption` endpoint. Build a serde_json::json!({}) body with chat_id, message_id, caption, parse_mode, and optionally reply_markup (parsed from string to Value).

decisions: Use JSON POST (not multipart) since no file upload needed for caption edits
reply_markup string is parsed with serde_json::from_str to embed as JSON value in the body

steps.task: Add `edit_message_media_raw` function in telegram_notify.rs. Signature: `pub async fn edit_message_media_raw(token: &str, chat_id: i64, message_id: i64, media_bytes: Vec<u8>, filename: String, media_type: &str, caption: &str, parse_mode: &str, reply_markup: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String>`. Uses reqwest multipart POST to Telegram `editMessageMedia`. The `media` field is a JSON string: `{"type": media_type, "media": "attach://file", "caption": caption, "parse_mode": parse_mode}`. The file is attached as a multipart part named `file`.

decisions: Use multipart because we're uploading a new file
media_type parameter allows reuse for both photo and video editing
knowledge.notes: The media JSON must reference 'attach://file' which corresponds to the multipart part name 'file'

steps.task: Add `edit_message_reply_markup_raw` function in telegram_notify.rs. Signature: `pub async fn edit_message_reply_markup_raw(token: &str, chat_id: i64, message_id: i64, reply_markup: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), String>`. Uses reqwest JSON POST to Telegram `editMessageReplyMarkup`. Pass reply_markup as parsed JSON value, or omit to remove all buttons.

knowledge.notes: Useful for removing buttons after publish, or updating button state

steps.task: Add callback query handler to the Telegram dispatcher in telegram.rs. Currently (lines 64-88) only `Update::filter_message()` is used. Add a second branch: `Update::filter_callback_query().endpoint(handle_callback_query)`. Add `handle_callback_query(bot: Bot, q: CallbackQuery, state: Arc<AppState>)` function that: (1) checks auth — q.message chat_id must match telegram_admin_chat_id, (2) extracts q.data string, (3) routes based on prefix: `aig_pub:`, `aig_cap:`, `aig_img:`, `aig_vid:`, `aig_sort:` to sub-handler functions (stub them as TODO for now), (4) calls `bot.answer_callback_query(q.id)` to dismiss the spinner. Import `CallbackQuery` from teloxide::types.

decisions: Callback data prefix convention: aig_ = artist instagram. Short prefixes to stay within Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit
Stub the sub-handlers as TODO — Phase 4 will implement them
Auth check: verify q.message.chat.id matches telegram_admin_chat_id
learnings: Current dispatcher at lines 64-88 only has Update::filter_message()
Auth check pattern exists at lines 94-115: checks telegram_admin_chat_id and telegram_topic_id
knowledge.notes: The handler tree should be: handler.branch(filter_message...).branch(filter_callback_query...). Use dptree::entry().endpoint(handle_callback_query)

steps.task: Add in-memory edit session state to AppState in main.rs. Define `EditSession` enum in telegram.rs with variants: `AwaitingCaption { artist_id: i64, preview_msg_id: i64 }`, `AwaitingImage { artist_id: i64, preview_msg_id: i64 }`, `AwaitingTimecode { artist_id: i64, track_number: u8, preview_msg_id: i64, video_msg_id: i64 }`. Add field `pub edit_sessions: Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<HashMap<i64, EditSession>>>` to AppState (keyed by user_id). Initialize as `Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new()))` in main(). Add `use std::collections::HashMap` if not already imported.

decisions: In-memory HashMap, lost on restart — acceptable since edit sessions are short-lived interactive UI flows
Key by user_id (from callback query), not chat_id, since multiple users could theoretically edit at once
Use tokio::sync::Mutex not std::sync::Mutex since we hold the lock across await points
learnings: AppState is at lines 51-67 of main.rs, now has edit_sessions field
EditSession enum defined in telegram.rs with 3 variants: AwaitingCaption, AwaitingImage, AwaitingTimecode
HashMap<i64, EditSession> imported via std::collections::HashMap already in main.rs
knowledge.notes: EditSession must be pub so telegram.rs handlers and the catch-all handler can access it

steps.task: Run `cargo check` from source/backend/ to verify Phase 1 compiles. Fix any compilation errors. The stub TODO handlers in step 6 should use `tracing::warn!("TODO: handle callback {}", data)` to avoid unused variable warnings.

learnings: All 7 implementation steps compile successfully with only dead-code warnings for the new unused functions (expected, will be used in later phases)
15 total warnings: 10 pre-existing + 4 dead-code for new functions + 1 unused import suggestion
knowledge.notes: Pre-existing warnings are acceptable, only new errors need fixing
